title: An Unusual Conch
description: The arthritic spider conch (Harpago arthriticus) is native to the shallow waters in the Indian and western Pacific oceans. The image is part of Jim Wehtje's upcoming exhibit at the Bailey-Matthews National Shell Museum in Sanibel, Florida. Wehtje is primarily an x-ray photographer of plants and shells, but this project gave him room to expand. "I thought my life would be making only x-ray images, but I dusted off the camera and found surface and color again," he told National Geographic.
translated_description: 关节炎蜘蛛螺（Harpago arthriticus）原产于印度洋和西太平洋的浅水区域。这张图片是吉姆·韦特杰即将在佛罗里达州萨尼贝尔的贝利-马修斯国家贝壳博物馆举办的展览中的一部分。韦特杰主要是一位植物和贝壳的X光摄影师，但这次项目给了他拓展的空间。“我曾以为我的生活只会拍摄X光图像，但我掸去了相机上的灰尘，重新发现了表面和色彩，”他告诉《国家地理》。
